extracted.intended_audience: general readers; students and practitioners of journalism, media studies, public relations, and communications
extracted.subtask_description: Identifying and applying techniques, practices, and contextual norms used to influence how information is presented and covered by news media. Covers tactics (e.g., timing, spin), institutional mechanisms (e.g., press releases, embargoes), values (e.g., objectivity, news values), and broader phenomena (e.g., propaganda, media capture).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — managing the news
rubrics_metrics.description: Managing the news is the deliberate influencing of the presentation of information within the news media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Often used in a negative sense; implies active shaping of publicity and coverage rather than passive reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of release / burying bad news
rubrics_metrics.description: Releasing information late on a Friday (or other timing strategies) to give journalists less time to pursue or highlight a story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: releasing bad news late on a Friday to reduce coverage; tactic used to lessen publicity for damaging information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staying on message
rubrics_metrics.description: Limiting questions and attention to a narrow scope favorable to the subject by consistently returning to prepared talking points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to control the narrative in interviews and briefings; reduces opportunities for reporters to explore damaging angles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spin
rubrics_metrics.description: Deliberate presentation or framing of information in a way that casts events or facts in a favorable light for a person or organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes running a 'spin room' after events; frequently produces sound bites and selective emphasis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press release
rubrics_metrics.description: An official statement issued to media to announce something or shape coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary PR tool for providing curated information, quotes, and framing to journalists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press conference / press scrum / press pool
rubrics_metrics.description: Events organized to present information and allow limited journalist access under controlled conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Can be staged to control who asks questions, what is shown, and what sound bites are available; press pool limits full access to a subset of reporters.

rubrics_metrics.name: News embargo
rubrics_metrics.description: An agreement to hold publication of information until a specified time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used by PR and news outlets to coordinate simultaneous reporting; can be used strategically to manage timing and context of coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: News leak
rubrics_metrics.description: The deliberate or accidental release of information to selected journalists or outlets to influence coverage or prompt investigative reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leaking can be used to test media reaction, shift attention, or damage rivals; selective leaks give advantage to chosen outlets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sound bite
rubrics_metrics.description: A brief, memorable phrase or quote designed to be easily reported and repeated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Crafted to summarize and frame complex issues quickly; prioritizes brevity and shareability over nuance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Propaganda
rubrics_metrics.description: Systematic dissemination of information, ideas, or rumors to influence public opinion or obscure the truth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Often state-led or campaign-oriented; overlaps with spin, disinformation, and targeted messaging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Framing
rubrics_metrics.description: Shaping how an issue is presented and what aspects are emphasized or downplayed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choice of language, metaphors, context and comparisons influences interpretation (e.g., crime framing vs. social determinants).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sensationalism
rubrics_metrics.description: Presenting news in a way that emphasizes shock, emotion, or scandal over substance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Drives attention and circulation but can distort facts and priorities; common in tabloids and some broadcast coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Infotainment / soft media
rubrics_metrics.description: Blending information with entertainment, prioritizing engagement and emotion over depth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Can lead to diminished informational quality and 'dumbing down' of important issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Churnalism
rubrics_metrics.description: News content heavily based on press releases and pre-packaged material rather than original reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Results from resource constraints in newsrooms; increases reliance on PR-supplied framing and facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: False balance
rubrics_metrics.description: Presenting two sides of an issue as equally valid when evidence or consensus does not support parity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Can mislead audiences by amplifying fringe views; arises from an attempt to appear impartial.

rubrics_metrics.name: News values (selection criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial criteria that determine story importance and placement—e.g., 'above the fold', 'man bites dog' (unusualness).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These values drive editorial judgment about what gets prominence; understanding them helps manage what will attract coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agenda-setting
rubrics_metrics.description: The process by which media emphasis on certain issues influences public perception of what is important.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actors can try to shape the media agenda to prioritize favorable topics or bury unfavorable ones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media capture / media plurality / editorial independence
rubrics_metrics.description: Structural conditions affecting whether media serve public interest or are controlled by political/economic actors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concentration of ownership, state influence, or advertiser pressure can erode independent reporting and facilitate news management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freedom of information / freedom of the press
rubrics_metrics.description: Legal and institutional protections enabling access to information and independent reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stronger FOI and press protections limit the ability of actors to withhold or manipulate information from public view.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source protection
rubrics_metrics.description: Safeguards and norms preserving confidentiality of journalists' information sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Crucial for investigative journalism; weakening source protection reduces journalists' ability to report on sensitive wrongdoing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Codes of ethics, fact-checking, corrections, spiking
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalistic standards and editorial practices intended to ensure accuracy and accountability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Robust fact-checking and willingness to correct errors reduce the effectiveness of manipulative tactics; 'spiking' (killing stories) is an editorial control that can be misused.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public relations and reputation management techniques
rubrics_metrics.description: A suite of tactics—euphemism, understatement, non-apology apologies, transfer, weasel words—used to manage public perception.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Often combined with timing, framing, and spin to deflect criticism and shape narratives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Astroturfing / influence-for-hire / paid advocacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Manufacturing apparently grassroots support or using paid agents to create the appearance of broad backing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deceptive tactic to manipulate public opinion and media coverage; blurs genuine grassroots signals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disinformation / fake news / deepfakes
rubrics_metrics.description: Deliberate creation and spread of false or manipulated content (including deepfake audio/video) to mislead audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Can be used to discredit opponents, spread confusion, or create false narratives; detection and verification efforts are countermeasures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Catch and kill / burying of scholars / corporate cover-ups
rubrics_metrics.description: Suppressing or purchasing exclusive rights to damaging stories to prevent publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used by powerful actors to quarantine damaging information from the public sphere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protest paradigm / recuperation / culture jamming
rubrics_metrics.description: Patterns in coverage and counter-tactics where protests or dissent are framed, marginalized, or co-opted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Media framing can trivialize protests (protest paradigm) or systems can recuperate dissent by absorbing it into mainstream narratives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media event / pseudo-event / media circus
rubrics_metrics.description: Staged events designed primarily to attract media attention rather than to convey substantive news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to create controlled spectacle and produce predictable coverage; diverts attention from other matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crowd manipulation / fearmongering / psychological tactics
rubrics_metrics.description: Techniques that exploit crowd psychology and emotions (e.g., fear, outrage) to influence public opinion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes targeted messaging, loaded language, and repeated exposure; effective but ethically fraught.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pay-for-content / promotional practices (advertorial, native advertising)
rubrics_metrics.description: Paid content that resembles editorial material and is intended to promote a brand or viewpoint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Can mislead audiences if not clearly disclosed; blurs lines between advertising and journalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tabloid techniques / yellow journalism
rubrics_metrics.description: Using lurid headlines, exaggeration, and gossip to maximize readership and attention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritizes engagement metrics over accuracy; often associated with celebrity and scandal coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification and research (countermeasures)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practices such as investigation, corroboration, and sourcing that journalists and watchdogs use to resist manipulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Robust research and verification reduce the success of many news-management techniques; essential for holding power to account.
